title: Gallic Empire
capsule: The Gallic Empire (Imperium Galliarum) was a breakaway Roman state that emerged in 260 when the general Postumus killed the son of Emperor Gallienus and claimed imperial authority over Gaul, Britain, and Hispania during the Crisis of the Third Century. Postumus (r. 260–269) consolidated effective rule and repelled Germanic incursions across the Rhine, governing with conventional Roman administrative structures and issuing his own coinage, but was killed by his own troops when he refused to allow them to sack Moguntiacum (Mainz). The Gallic Empire ended in 274 when Aurelian defeated the last emperor Tetricus I at the Battle of Châlons, reintegrating the western provinces into a briefly reunified Roman Empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Gallic Empire's core provinces in Gaul and Britain are well attested through coin finds and epigraphy; whether Hispania remained under consistent Gallic control throughout is debated.
